$comment: Catalogue of LaTeX table fragments, rendered by _scripts/export_neo4j_table.py into semio Table windows. Queries are read-only and must return 'left' and 'right' columns — the semio two-column table API (\SemioTableTwo) takes exactly two. Use this instead of a diagram when the relationship is a set of numbers: a fan-in from a few sources to many targets reads as a table and as a hairball as a graph.

tables.name: huerden-traeger
tables.title: Träger der Hürden
tables.description: How many Bauteilgruppen and Projekte carry each barrier — the companion to the huerden figure
tables.$comment: German naming mirrors the display map in views.json → huerden. Keep the two in step.
tables.cypher:
MATCH (h:Huerde)
OPTIONAL MATCH (bg:Bauteilgruppe)-[:HAT_HUERDE]->(h)
WITH h, count(DISTINCT bg) AS bauteilgruppen
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Projekt)-[:HAT_HUERDE]->(h)
WITH h, bauteilgruppen, count(DISTINCT p) AS projekte
RETURN CASE h.name
         WHEN 'Witterung_Feuchte'          THEN 'Witterung / Feuchte'
         WHEN 'Verfuegbarkeitsproblem'     THEN 'Verfügbarkeitsproblem'
         WHEN 'Heterogenitaet_Chargen'     THEN 'Heterogenität der Chargen'
         WHEN 'Unkonventionelles_Material' THEN 'Unkonventionelles Material'
         WHEN 'Fehlende_Lagerflaeche'      THEN 'Fehlende Lagerfläche'
         ELSE replace(h.name, '_', ' ') END AS left,
       toString(bauteilgruppen) + ' / ' + toString(projekte) AS right
ORDER BY bauteilgruppen + projekte DESC
